subject: POC plan: multilingual model shortlist & fallback approach
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Wong <lisa.wong@finpay.com>, Rajesh Patel <rajesh@finpay.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: POC plan: multilingual model shortlist & fallback approach

Hi Lisa / Rajesh —

Thanks again for a productive call this morning. Recap and proposed next steps below so we all have the same playbook for the 4-week technical trial:

Quick recap
- Goal: validate an LLM-powered customer support assistant that can handle English, Spanish, and French for Tier 1 email triage + short responses (templates + suggested replies).
- Primary constraints: sub-250ms 95th latency for n=50 concurrent users (target for real-time UI), maintain >88% intent classification accuracy on your closed prompt set, and keep inference cost within the budget range we discussed.

Proposed POC plan (high level) — 4 weeks
1) Week 0 (this week): finalize scope, access + security checklist, and sign off on data samples & prompt set.
2) Week 1: baseline evaluations — run our model shortlist on your prompt set, gather latency/cost/accuracy.
3) Week 2: runway testing (load + prefix/KV cache tuning), and quantization comparisons.
4) Week 3: A/B eval on 2 shortlisted models for quality; run multilingual edge-cases.
5) Week 4: final recommendation + handoff doc and ops playbook.

Model shortlist for trial
- Candidate A (primary): Mistral-Instruct-12B (full FP16 on Redwood Dedicated) — best quality/cost balance for instruction output.
- Candidate B (alternate): Llama-3-13B-chat (8-bit quant, optimized kernel path) — stronger on instruction-following, slightly higher cost.
- Fallback: Llama-2-7B-quant (local fallback variant; cheaper and smaller for on-device/edge fallback).

Multilingual notes
- We'll run the English prompt set directly plus translated variants for Spanish/French. For safety, include a short bilingual prompt test set (50 examples each) to validate hallucination rates.

Success criteria (initial proposal)
- Latency: 95th percentile < 250ms for 1-2 token streaming responses; 95th < 400ms for 32-token responses.
- Quality: intent classification F1 >= 0.88 on your labeled set; generation BLEU/ROUGE will be secondary — human-rated acceptability >= 85% on the sample pool.
- Cost: projected inference cost <= $0.50 per 1k user interactions at target throughput (we'll refine after baseline run).

Ownership & next steps
- Redwood: Evelyn (AE, owner) + Markus (solutions engineer) + Marissa (eval lead) — will run baselines and provide tuning recommendations.
- FinPay: Lisa (product owner) + Rajesh (platform) — provide prompt set, sample data, and access for testing.

Actions (for this week):
- Lisa: share 300 prompt examples + 50 bilingual edge cases and SRE contact for testing VPC access (by Wed EOD).
- Redwood: send security checklist and POA&M; we'll provision test endpoints on Dedicated and a fallback private variant.

Attachments: finpay_requirements_v1.pdf (your doc from today), poc-metrics-template.xlsx (blank template we use for scoring).

If that looks right, reply with formal sign-off and we'll schedule a 30-min kickoff with Markus for Thursday.

Thanks —
Evelyn

Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: POC plan: multilingual model shortlist & fallback approach

Thanks, Evelyn — this looks great and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications: 

- Budget: our infra budget cap for inference during the trial is $9k total. If projections exceed that after your baseline run, we'll discuss scope adjustments.
- Data: we can share the 300 prompts by Wednesday; note that some prompts include account-specific entities (masked ok).
- Compliance: Rajesh will handle the VPC onboarding; he prefers ssh key-based access + a short runbook for evidence we can hand to our security team.

One ask on the model shortlist: can you also include a small test of Mistral-7B-chat (if available) as a super-low-cost quality baseline? If it’s cheap to spin up, we want to see the delta vs the 12B/13B runs.

We sign off to kickoff once we see the security checklist and a tentative slot for kickoff.

—Lisa

Subject: Re: POC plan: multilingual model shortlist & fallback approach

Thanks — adding my plan for baseline runs and what I'll need from FinPay.

Baseline plan (Markus)\- Provision 3 endpoints on Redwood Dedicated (Mistral-12B FP16, Llama-3-13B 8-bit, Mistral-7B FP16) and a fallback Llama-2-7B-quant instance on our private pool.
- Run prompt set across models: record latency distribution (p50/p90/p95), token-level cost, and a lightweight quality score (automated intent classifier + sampling of 150 human reviews across languages).
- Run quantization comparison for Llama-3 to see if 8-bit gives acceptable quality degradation.

Dependencies from FinPay\- Sample prompt set (300) + bilingual edge cases (50 each)
- Any rate-limiting rules (e.g., max tokens per interaction)
- Contact for VPC/test network access

Deliverables by end of Week 1\- Baseline report (latency/cost/automated quality)
- Suggested config: batching window, KV cache TTL, recommended model for each language

Notes: I'll attach the baseline run command snippets and the lightweight eval harness to the sharepoint link after kickoff. Also, Markus will own the A/B traffic split during Week 3.

-Markus

Subject: Re: POC plan: multilingual model shortlist & fallback approach

Quick note on evaluation and success metrics — I'm attaching the scoring rubric in the sheet you received. Highlights: 

Evaluation plan details (Marissa)\- Test sets: English (300), Spanish (50), French (50), bilingual edge-cases (150) 
- Metrics: Intent F1, generation acceptability (human-rated 1-5), hallucination flag rate, latency percentiles.
- A/B methodology: Week 3 we'll route 40/40/20 traffic across (Mistral-12B / Llama-3-13B / fallback) to gather comparable production-like signals.
- Tolerance gates: if hallucination flag rate > 12% in any language, halt rollout and apply prompt-engineering + system prompt whitelist.

I recommend we include automated post-processing to redact account-specific PII during the eval runs so results are shareable. I can coordinate with Rajesh on that flow.

Deliverable schedule (revised)
- End Week 1: scoring CSV + baseline report
- Mid Week 2: cache & batching tuning results
- End Week 3: A/B result summary + recommended model selection
- Week 4: ops playbook & handoff

I'll also add a short human-raters guide so FinPay can replicate scoring after handoff.

-Marissa
